briefings.title: Bank Earnings Are In: Here’s What They’re REALLY Saying About the U.S. Economy | The Weekly Wrap
briefings.tldr: Despite fears of a private credit downturn, latest earnings from major banks show "benign" credit quality and a resilient U.S. economy, suggesting no imminent recession even as AI disruption looms over the software sector.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Despite fears of a private credit downturn, latest earnings from major banks show "benign" credit quality and a resilient U.S. economy, suggesting no imminent recession even as AI disruption looms over the software sector.

## State of the U.S. Credit Cycle & Economy
*   **Credit Quality Benchmarks:** To gauge the economy, Eisman focuses on "non-accruing loans" (loans delinquent by 90+ days) at the four largest banks.
    *   **J.P. Morgan:** Non-accruals were $9.6 billion, up 11% year-over-year but down 3% sequentially from Q4.
    *   **Bank of America:** Total non-accruals were $5.8 billion, down 4% year-over-year and flat compared to Q4.
*   **Economic Resilience:** There is currently no data supporting a broad credit cycle or recession. While the economy is "K-shaped" (not fine for everyone), the banking data suggests the overall U.S. economy remains powerful.
*   **Geopolitical Impact:** Despite the breakdown of U.S.-Iran talks and the blocking of the Strait of Hormuz, markets remain optimistic about a settlement. Oil briefly spiked above $100 but retreated, and the S&P 500 has returned to record highs.

## Major Bank Earnings Analysis
*   **Investment-Centric Outperformance:** Diversified firms (Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, JPM) generally outperformed lending-centric banks (Wells Fargo, Bank of America).
    *   **Morgan Stanley:** Labeled "best-in-class" this quarter with a 27% return on tangible common equity (ROTCE), the highest in the industry.
    *   **Goldman Sachs:** Reported a massive 21% ROTCE, driven by an 89% year-over-year increase in advisory revenue, though fixed income trading was a "disappointment" (down 10%).
    *   **Citigroup:** Showing signs of a turnaround under Jane Fraser with a 13% ROTCE, its best in years, leading to a valuation re-rating to 1.3x tangible book value.
*   **Lending Headwinds:**
    *   **Wells Fargo:** Disappointed the market with a 13-basis point sequential decline in net interest margin. Net interest income (NII) remains a primary driver of earnings for lending-heavy banks.
    *   **Valuation Gap:** Lending-centric banks trade at lower multiples (1.8x–1.9x tangible book) compared to investment-heavy banks (~3x tangible book) because lending is highly competitive and net interest margins are in long-term decline.

## Private Credit & Regional Bank Risks
*   **Regional Bank Exposure:** Contrary to some market fears, regional banks (represented by the KRE ETF) have very little exposure to private credit. 
*   **Concentrated Risk:** Private credit exposure is concentrated in the 32 largest financial institutions. 
    *   **Disclosed Exposures:** J.P. Morgan ($50B), Wells Fargo ($36B), and Citi ($22B).
    *   **Subordination Protections:** Most bank loans to the private credit sector are senior with roughly 40% loss cushions, meaning the underlying assets must lose significant value before the banks suffer capital hits.
*   **New Opportunities:** Firms like Blackstone and Goldman are raising new $10B funds. These are attractive because they are "clean"—they lack the problematic software loan exposure found in older private credit portfolios.

## Emerging Risks: AI and Software
*   **Structural Threat:** AI poses a multi-faceted threat to the software sector that may take over a year to clarify.
    *   **Decreased Barriers:** Concerns that AI will allow customers to build internal custom software rather than purchasing external solutions.
    *   **Pricing Power:** Potential for AI to permanently erode the ability of software companies to raise prices.
*   **Investment Strategy:** Eisman advises "treading carefully" with the software group. It is difficult to predict a bottom when the narrative has turned so aggressively negative.

## Notable Quotes
> "As the banks go, so goes the economy. Until credit quality changes, the U.S. economy will be fine." — **Steve Eisman**

> "Lending is highly, highly competitive... as a result, net interest margins have been in long-term decline for years and that has put pressure on returns." — **Steve Eisman**

> "If and when losses appear [in private credit], this will be an income statement problem, but not a systemic capital problem." — **Steve Eisman**

briefings.title: Coffee with Crow: Building A Future Where Everyone Can Work with AI | ASU+GSV Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: To prevent a repeat of the "China shock" displacement of the 1980s, the U.S. must establish a "grand bargain" where employers and universities co-design a continuous, "K to grey" learning system that prioritizes individual empowerment over shareholder-only gains.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
To prevent a repeat of the "China shock" displacement of the 1980s, the U.S. must establish a "grand bargain" where employers and universities co-design a continuous, "K to grey" learning system that prioritizes individual empowerment over shareholder-only gains.

## The "Grand Bargain" for Workforce Security
*   **Addressing Public Anxiety:** Gina Raimondo notes that over 70% of Americans fear AI-driven job loss. She warns that failing to address this anxiety with a concrete plan will lead to political over-regulation that stifles U.S. competitiveness.
*   **The Employer Mandate:** Companies must transition from being passive consumers of talent to active drivers of the education system.
    *   **Skill Definition:** Employers must continuously define the skills needed for today and tomorrow.
    *   **Bridging the Gap:** Unlike the manufacturing shift to China, which left millions without a path to the service economy, the AI transition requires a "bridge" for workers of all ages to pivot.
*   **Continuous Learning:** Education can no longer be a "one-and-done" event; it must be a lifetime of continuous upskilling to match the pace of technological change.

## Transforming Higher Education: The "CEO" Model
*   **Institutional Inertia:** Sethuraman Panchanathan argues that universities are currently too slow and remain in denial, often settling for "adaptation" when "transformation" is required.
*   **The Five Pillars of Co-Creation:** Panchanathan proposes a "CEO" mindset (Collaboration, Innovation, and Transformation) based on:
    *   **Co-creation & Co-design:** Developing curriculum alongside industry leaders.
    *   **Co-habitation:** Eliminating the "four walls" of the university to embed faculty and students within real-world industry environments.
    *   **Co-evolution:** Updating the roles of tenure-track faculty to include practitioners and "professors of practice" who live in the real world.
*   **Democratizing Opportunity:** While talent is universal, opportunity is not; universities must leverage AI to scale access to elite learning resources for the "massive" population rather than just the "best and brightest."

## AI as a Tool for Student Success
*   **The Three Competencies:** Marie Lynn Miranda outlines three pillars every student must possess to survive the AI era:
    *   **Fluency:** The ability to incorporate AI into sophisticated process workflows.
    *   **Criticality:** Understanding the limitations of Large Language Models (LLMs), specifically how they miss information on the "tails" of distribution and can be manipulated.
    *   **Ethics:** Knowing when to disclose AI use and identifying inherent biases in data models.
*   **AI-Informed Data Science:** The University of Illinois Chicago uses data science to proactively support first-generation students.
    *   **Predictive Support:** By analyzing non-cognitive assets (e.g., financial stability, support networks) and academic history, the university provides tutoring *before* a student fails a midterm.
    *   **Eliminating Rote Work:** AI is used to handle administrative data entry for advisors, freeing them to focus on high-impact, one-on-one human transformation.

## Principled Innovation and the "Agentic Self"
*   **Individual Empowerment:** Michael Crow argues that the "tech-bro" narrative of a "Death Star" AI replacing humans is heartless. Instead, the focus should be on creating an "agentic self"—using AI as a personal enabler to help individuals make better decisions and project their ideas.
*   **The Moral Imperative:** Advancing science without a democratic purpose is viewed as an amoral act.
    *   **Liberty to Learn:** Technology should be used to advance the "individual liberty" of the worker and the success of the family unit.
    *   **The Veil of Ignorance:** Crow suggests a new philosophy where AI provides "unlimited equal opportunity" by acting as a personalized learning assistant for every human being, regardless of their starting point in life.

## Notable Quotes

> "If AI creates America's first trillionaire... and millions of the rest of us are left behind, that's not a success. That's horrific for a democracy; it certainly makes us less competitive." — **Gina Raimondo**

> "We have to reverse the logic that the 'tech bros' are talking about—this sort of 'Death Star' image of a tool that's going to replace everyone. If we do this right, each person is going to be individually and personally empowered." — **Michael M. Crow**

> "Entry-level jobs will still exist. The requirements for those entry-level jobs are changing significantly, and universities have an obligation to make sure we’re equipping people with the skills they need." — **Marie Lynn Miranda**

> "Universities today are too slow and they are in denial... What is required is a mindset shift or a paradigm shift. It can be done, it should be done, and it must be done." — **Sethuraman Panchanathan**

briefings.title: Demis Hassabis Wants to Build AGI. Should We Trust Him?
briefings.tldr: Demis Hassabis, the Nobel-winning founder of DeepMind, is driven by a unique blend of scientific rigor and "spiritual" ambition to build AGI, balancing a high-stakes rivalry with OpenAI against his desire to remain a "good" steward of humanity's most powerful invention.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Demis Hassabis, the Nobel-winning founder of DeepMind, is driven by a unique blend of scientific rigor and "spiritual" ambition to build AGI, balancing a high-stakes rivalry with OpenAI against his desire to remain a "good" steward of humanity's most powerful invention.

## The Evolution of a "Jedi" Polymath
* **A Diverse Background:** Hassabis’s journey to the top of Google’s AI efforts began as a child chess prodigy (ranking 2nd in the world for his age) and a video game designer of the hit *Theme Park* at age 17.
    * **Parental Influence:** His character is defined by a tension between his mother’s Christian values of compassion and his father’s "win-at-all-costs" competitive drive.
    * **Academic Range:** Unlike many Silicon Valley leaders, Hassabis is a deep scientist, holding a PhD in neuroscience which he used to model artificial intelligence after the human brain’s "action and perception" mechanisms.
* **Charisma and Control:** Journalist Sebastian Mallaby describes Hassabis as having a "Jedi" quality—an ability to stare people in the eye and make them believe his vision for the future.
    * **The "Good vs. Great" Conflict:** While Hassabis strives to be a moral leader, Mallaby notes a "blind spot" regarding his controlling nature, evidenced by the 2019 departure of co-founder Mustafa Suleyman.

## Scientific Breakthroughs: From Atari to the Nobel Prize
* **The Core Innovation:** DeepMind’s early success was built on fusing two distinct AI traditions:
    * **Deep Learning:** Identifying patterns in massive datasets.
    * **Reinforcement Learning:** Learning through experience and feedback (trial and error).
* **AlphaGo to AlphaFold:** After defeating the world champion in the game of Go, Hassabis immediately pivoted to biology, recognizing that the "combinatorial space" of games was the perfect training ground for scientific discovery.
    * **AlphaFold Success:** By solving the 50-year-old "protein folding" problem, DeepMind provided a tool to the global scientific community that is now accelerating drug discovery and medicine.
    * **Algorithmic Invention:** Mallaby argues this proves AI labs are doing deep "algorithmic invention," not just scaling up data centers.
* **Open Science:** In a show of "virtue ethics," Hassabis made the AlphaFold database open-source and free for all scientists worldwide.

## The OpenAI Rivalry and the LLM Blind Spot
* **Missing the Language Wave:** Despite DeepMind being the "OG" of AI labs, they were caught off guard by ChatGPT. 
    * **The Gaia Project:** Hassabis was focused on "Gaia," a simulation of the natural world, believing AGI required an agent to act in physical space rather than just processing "symbols" (language). 
    * **Shift in Strategy:** The release of GPT-3 in 2020 forced Hassabis to pivot DeepMind's resources toward Large Language Models (LLMs) to catch up with OpenAI.
* **Perceptions of Rivals:** According to Mallaby, Hassabis views his competitors through specific lenses:
    * **Sam Altman:** Driven primarily by the pursuit of power.
    * **Mark Zuckerberg:** Driven by shareholder value and product addiction.
    * **Elon Musk:** Seen as a "hypocritical" figure who oscillates between "doomsterism" and aggressive acceleration.

## Existential Risk and the "Spiritual" Quest
* **AGI as Faith:** Hassabis views the quest for superintelligence as a spiritual endeavor akin to "the God of Spinoza"—the idea that understanding nature through science brings one closer to the divine.
* **The Probability of Doom (P-Doom):** While Hassabis remains "cautiously optimistic," the briefing highlights a growing concern regarding AI safety.
    * **The Survival Instinct:** Geoffrey Hinton argues that we may accidentally grant AI a survival instinct by tasking it with defending itself against cyberattacks. 
    * **The "Race Condition":** There is a persistent tension between Hassabis's safety principles and the market pressure to release "open-weight" models (like Google’s Gemma) to compete with rivals.
* **Conclusion on Character:** Mallaby concludes that Hassabis is "both great and good," but acknowledges that the "greatness" of the task often requires a pragmatism that can conflict with pure moral idealism.

## Notable Quotes
> "If you're right... it follows that you as the creator of AI will be one of the most important people in the history of humanity, which means you don't have a choice. Somebody's going to write a book about you." — **Sebastian Mallaby** (recalling his pitch to Hassabis)

> "He [Hassabis] is the only person who was really at the origin of the science and also a lab leader... Sam Altman, not a scientist, dropped out of Stanford, very different kettle of fish." — **Sebastian Mallaby**

> "We are defined by the desire to invent as human beings and he [Hassabis] is part of that and he is leading us on a frightening ride, but it's kind of human destiny to go there." — **Sebastian Mallaby**

> "You put those three things together: superintelligence, survival instinct, and devious obfuscation. It feels like analytically I can't be confident that we're not going to be attacked." — **Sebastian Mallaby** (on the risks of AGI)

briefings.title: Did JD Vance Just Blow Up His 2028 Run? | Pivot
briefings.channel: Pivot with Kara Swisher and Scott Galloway

people.name: JD Vance
people.role: Vice President of the United States

briefings.tldr: While global geopolitical tensions escalate, the stock market remains dislocated from consumer reality; meanwhile, Anthropic has overtaken OpenAI in revenue momentum as Amazon positions itself to challenge Starlink’s satellite dominance.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** While global geopolitical tensions escalate, the stock market remains dislocated from consumer reality; meanwhile, Anthropic has overtaken OpenAI in revenue momentum as Amazon positions itself to challenge Starlink’s satellite dominance.

## Geopolitical Tensions and Market Dislocation
* **Conflict in the Middle East:** Despite Iranian threats to the Red Sea and a U.S. blockade of Iranian ports, markets remain resilient.
    * **Strait of Hormuz:** Scott Galloway supports a U.S. threat to block the Strait entirely to maintain the principle of freedom of navigation, noting that allowing regional powers to block global transit sets a dangerous precedent.
* **Economic Decoupling:** The S&P 500 rose 2.8% during the taping, reflecting a "dislocation" between market performance and the lived experience of average Americans.
    * **The Wealth Gap:** The top decile of Americans now owns 90% of stocks and is responsible for 50% of consumer spending.
    * **Inflationary Pressures:** While the wealthy remain unaffected, the lower half of the country is struggling with gasoline prices (up 36%) and Brent crude (up 32%).
* **Energy Independence:** U.S. energy independence has allowed the domestic market to ignore oil shocks that are currently devastating European benchmarks.

## The AI Power Shift: Anthropic vs. OpenAI
* **Revenue Momentum:** Anthropic has reportedly tripled its Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) in just four months, growing from $9 billion to $30 billion. 
    * **OpenAI Lagging:** OpenAI’s ARR stands at approximately $25 billion, marking the first time Anthropic has led on revenue.
* **Enterprise vs. Consumer Strategy:** 80% of Anthropic’s revenue is enterprise-driven, which Galloway argues is a more stable and higher-margin business than OpenAI’s 40% enterprise share.
* **The Microsoft Fracture:** OpenAI is publicly distancing itself from Microsoft, claiming the partnership limits its ability to meet enterprise needs, while "bear-hugging" Amazon. 
    * **Leadership Critique:** Galloway suggests OpenAI is "burning up on re-entry," citing public tiffs with Microsoft and a 27% chance (via prediction markets) that Sam Altman will be replaced as CEO by year-end.

## Amazon’s $11.5B Satellite Play
* **Globalstar Acquisition:** Amazon is acquiring satellite operator Globalstar to bolster "Project LEO" (formerly Project Kuiper), aiming to become the "strongest infrastructure company in the world."
    * **Catching Starlink:** Amazon currently has 240 operational satellites compared to Starlink’s 10,000+. Amazon plans to deploy 3,200 by 2029.
    * **Strategic Infrastructure:** Beyond consumer Wi-Fi, the network will support Amazon’s internal B2B needs, including warehouses, delivery hubs, and autonomous drones.
* **"Amazon Prime Plus":** Galloway predicts Amazon will eventually launch a phone and a "Prime Plus" tier, offering lightning-fast home and mobile connectivity to its 115 million subscriber households.

## Political and Corporate Maneuvering
* **Airlines Merger:** United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby has reportedly pitched a merger with American Airlines directly to Donald Trump.
    * **Market Concentration:** A combined entity would control 40% of U.S. domestic capacity. Galloway calls the proposal "antitrust nightmare" and "ridiculous," noting it would leave only one or two carriers on 289 overlapping routes.
* **Jerome Powell vs. Trump:** Trump continues to threaten to fire Fed Chair Jerome Powell, despite Powell's term lasting until 2028. Galloway views these attacks as "distractions" from negative news cycles.
* **JD Vance and the Pope:** Vice President Vance criticized the Pope for speaking on "theology" regarding peace. Swisher and Galloway noted this is a "politically stupid" move that risks alienating swing-voting Evangelicals and Catholics.

## Financial Policy and Predictions
* **Trump "Baby Bonds":** Five million children have signed up for Trump accounts featuring $1,000 seed deposits. Galloway supports the concept of "baby bonds" but suggests they should be locked until age 65 to eventually replace Social Security.
* **Prediction: The "AI Pivot" Bubble:** Galloway predicts a wave of failing companies will rebrand as AI firms to trigger short-term stock pops.
    * **Case Study:** Allbirds (rebranded as NewBird AI) saw a 900% intraday spike after announcing a pivot to leasing GPUs. Galloway warns that copycats like Chegg or GameStop may follow, leading to significant retail investor losses.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "The stock market is now a proxy for companies that are mostly invested in technology and some oil companies... wealthy people just aren't affected [by gas prices]." — **Scott Galloway**

> "I think he’s [JD Vance] torpedoing his 2026 chances by picking a fight [with the Pope]... the Pope is talking about peace, he’s talking about tyrants, he’s talking about everything Jesus talked about." — **Kara Swisher**

> "Anthropic has more momentum than any company in the world right now... the little engine that was an afterthought to OpenAI 12 months ago is now a bigger business." — **Scott Galloway**

> "When you’re the market leader... you never reference the competition. When you reference the competition, you’re immediately saying they’re a competitor. OpenAI looks like they're flailing." — **Scott Galloway**

briefings.title: FULL BRIEFING: IMFC Chair Al Jadaan And Kristalina Georgieva Hold Spring Meetings | DRM News | AF1F

people.name: Mohammed Al-Jadaan
people.role: Chair, International Monetary and Financial Committee (IMFC)

briefings.tldr: The global economy faces a "new normal" of persistent uncertainty driven by Middle East conflicts and supply disruptions, prompting the IMF to call for fiscal discipline and the adoption of the landmark "Daria Principles" to reform fund governance for the first time in 15 years.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The global economy faces a "new normal" of persistent uncertainty driven by Middle East conflicts and supply disruptions, prompting the IMF to call for fiscal discipline and the adoption of the landmark "Daria Principles" to reform fund governance for the first time in 15 years.

## Geopolitical Risks and Energy Stability
* **The "Slow-Moving Vessel" Crisis:** Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva warned that supply disruptions in the Middle East are cumulative; every day tankers are delayed adds at least 40 days to delivery cycles, impacting not just oil and gas but also fertilizers and naphtha.
* **Escalation Scenarios:** While the IMF’s baseline scenario assumes a short-lived conflict with modest growth hits, prolonged instability risks a "more adverse scenario" characterized by lower growth and higher inflation.
* **Physical vs. Paper Markets:** Minister Aljadaan noted a "serious disconnect" between the paper market (speculative trading) and the physical market. 
    * De-escalation signals (like the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz) may cool paper prices, but physical stability requires insurance companies to resume coverage and tanker owners to commit to the region.
* **Infrastructure Recovery:** Impacted countries have varying recovery timelines; some have restored production quickly, while others face long-term damage to energy assets.

## Landmark IMF Governance Reforms
* **The Daria Principles:** Members unanimously adopted the first major quota and governance reforms in over 15 years.
* **Fair Representation:** The principles aim to increase transparency and fairness in quota reviews, ensuring regional balance at the Executive Board.
* **Leadership Selection:** The process for selecting the Managing Director will now officially uphold open, inclusive, merit-based, and transparent procedures.
* **Protecting Vulnerable Nations:** A core tenet of the reform is the protection of voting shares and quotas for low-income countries.

## Monetary and Fiscal Policy Mandates
* **Fiscal Prudence:** The IMF cautioned against "untargeted measures" such as broad-based tax cuts or export controls, which could prolong inflation. 
    * **Policy Advice:** Governments are urged to implement "targeted, temporary, and timely" measures to support the most vulnerable without undermining debt sustainability.
* **Central Bank Commitment:** Central banks remain "laser-focused" on price stability. 
    * **Balance of Risks:** Policymakers must carefully calibrate the timing of interest rate adjustments to avoid tightening too soon or waiting too long.
* **Structural Reforms:** Leaders emphasized that strong growth via productivity-improving reforms is the best "shock absorber" for a world prone to frequent disruptions.

## Financial Support and Global Outreach
* **Program Augmentation:** Approximately 12 countries have indicated a need for additional support. The IMF estimates potential program augmentations and new financing could range between **$20 billion and $50 billion**.
* **PRGT Funding:** Georgieva issued an urgent call to fully fund the Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust (PRGT) to support low-income and fragile states during this period of high interest rates and debt vulnerability.
* **Venezuela Re-engagement:** After a seven-year pause, a majority of the membership has voted to resume relations with Venezuela. The IMF will coordinate with the World Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank to help the country achieve macroeconomic stability.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "Persistent [uncertainty] does not mean paralysis. It is our hope that peace will soon be restored around the world... countries need to strengthen their resilience by being agile, proactive, and implementing necessary reforms." — **Minister Mohammed Aljadaan**

> "A tanker is a slow-moving vessel. Every day tankers are not leaving adds at least 40 days to the first delivery. And that translates into shortage not only of oil and gas, but also of naphtha and fertilizers." — **Kristalina Georgieva**

> "Despite the movements in the paper market, people want to find oil and gas and they are willing to pay significantly more as we speak. I think the challenge today is not how much production can be ramped up—it’s really the logistics and the assurances that the waters are clear." — **Minister Mohammed Aljadaan**

> "This is not a moment for untargeted measures such as export controls or broad-based tax cuts, which may only prolong the pain of high prices." — **Kristalina Georgieva**

briefings.title: How to prove who's human online (ft. Ben Horowitz and Alex Blania)
briefings.tldr: As AI capabilities outpace traditional bot detection, World (formerly Worldcoin) proposes iris-based biometric verification as the only scalable, privacy-preserving method to distinguish unique humans from autonomous agents in an increasingly deepfaked digital economy.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
As AI capabilities outpace traditional bot detection, World (formerly Worldcoin) proposes iris-based biometric verification as the only scalable, privacy-preserving method to distinguish unique humans from autonomous agents in an increasingly deepfaked digital economy.

## The Escalating Crisis of Digital Personhood
*   **The "1% Glimpse":** Alex Blania (CEO of World) warns that current bot activity is less than 1% of what is coming; as the cost of intelligence drops, AI agents will become superhuman in their ability to manipulate and "program" humans.
*   **Identity Categories:** The internet is shifting from a binary (human/bot) to a three-tier interaction model:
    *   **Humans:** Unique biological individuals.
    *   **Human-Directed Agents:** AI acting with specific permissions on behalf of a human.
    *   **Autonomous Agents:** Purely AI-driven entities with their own agendas.
*   **The Failure of Digital Signals:** Previous "Web of Trust" models (relying on GitHub history or social media longevity) are now obsolete. AI can easily forge years of digital history and "attest" to the humanity of other AI accounts, creating self-validating bot networks.

## Why Conventional Solutions Fall Short
*   **The Entropy Problem:** Standard biometrics like FaceID or fingerprints work for 1-to-1 authentication (checking if you are the same person who owns the phone). However, they lack the mathematical entropy required for 1-to-N uniqueness (checking if you are a unique human not already in the system). FaceID "hits a wall" after tens of millions of users, whereas the iris provides enough information to scale to billions.
*   **Government ID Limitations:** Relying on state-issued IDs is dismissed due to:
    *   **Privacy Risks:** Instant loss of anonymity and the danger of centralized government surveillance.
    *   **Fragmentation:** Government systems are not globally interoperable; a "perfect" system in Singapore does not help a platform like Meta manage 3 billion global users.
*   **Replay Attacks:** Digital-only verification is vulnerable to deepfakes injected directly into camera streams. World argues that custom hardware (the Orb) is necessary to verify physical presence through multi-spectral sensors that can distinguish a real eye from a high-resolution screen.

## World’s Technical and Privacy Architecture
*   **Privacy-Preserving Verification:** To avoid a "centralized database of eyeballs," World utilizes two primary cryptographic techniques:
    *   **Multi-Party Computation (MPC):** The iris code is broken into fragments and distributed across multiple independent computers. No single entity ever possesses the full biometric template.
    *   **Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKP):** Users hold a "secret" on their phones. They can prove to a third-party platform (like Reddit or X) that they are a unique human verified by the MPC system without ever revealing their biometric data or real-world identity.
*   **Hardware Evolution:** The Orb has transitioned from a "wild" futuristic concept to a necessary utility. Blania notes that iris scanning is becoming normalized through devices like the Apple Vision Pro.

## Macro Applications: From Dating to Democracy
*   **Economic Integrity:** Ben Horowitz notes that $400 billion was stolen during COVID stimulus programs due to identity fraud. Cryptographic "proof of human" is essential for the efficient distribution of Universal Basic Income (UBI) or social services.
*   **Protecting Democracy:** Current systems (like mail-in ballots and Social Security numbers) are vulnerable to AI-scale fraud. Without proof of human, high-scale impersonation could render the "will of the people" impossible to determine.
*   **Consumer Use Cases:** 
    *   **Dating:** Tinder is testing World ID in Japan to ensure users are interacting with authentic humans.
    *   **Video Conferencing:** As deepfakes become real-time and photorealistic, high-value users (e.g., fund managers) will need to cryptographically verify their identity on calls.
    *   **Gaming:** Preventing AI from "destroying" human players in competitive environments where money or status is at stake.

## Scaling and the US Market
*   **Current Scale:** The project currently has **18 million verified users** and 40 million total app users.
*   **US Focus:** After navigating regulatory uncertainty, the company is shifting 90% of its effort to the US. The goal is to deploy **50,000 Orbs** to ensure every American is within 15 minutes of a device.
*   **Distribution Innovations:** 
    *   **Partnerships:** Potential deployments in high-traffic locations like Starbucks or coffee shops.
    *   **Orb on Demand:** A pilot program for the Bay Area and NYC where an Orb can be delivered via motorbike to a user’s location within 15 minutes for verification.

> "AIs are really good at programming humans. Much better than humans are at programming AIs." — **Alex Blania**

> "In a world of AI, having a human network is going to be this incredibly important thing. There's a massive network effect... people are starting six years behind [World] on that." — **Ben Horowitz**

> "Honestly, if you don't take it serious now, then I think you just should get a different job... what we currently see is less than 1% of what it will look like in probably a year or two." — **Alex Blania**

briefings.title: LIVE: Howard Lutnick and Lilly CEO David Ricks expected to speak at Semafor summit
briefings.tldr: The U.S. is pivoting toward an aggressive "Build in America" industrial policy, targeting 6% GDP growth through massive domestic infrastructure investment and strategic equity stakes in tech companies, while simultaneously racing to lead the "Genesis Mission" of AI-driven scientific discovery and the commercialization of space and fusion energy.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The U.S. is pivoting toward an aggressive "Build in America" industrial policy, targeting 6% GDP growth through massive domestic infrastructure investment and strategic equity stakes in tech companies, while simultaneously racing to lead the "Genesis Mission" of AI-driven scientific discovery and the commercialization of space and fusion energy.

## The New American Industrial Policy
* **GDP Growth Strategy:** U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick projects reaching 6% GDP growth by 2027-2028, driven by an $18 trillion "build" initiative.
    * **Shovel-Ready Goals:** Lutnick argues that getting "shovels in the ground" for chip fabs (like Micron and TSMC) and drug onshoring ($400 billion) will naturally drive growth regardless of traditional economic skepticism.
* **The "Benefit of the Bargain" Model:** The government is shifting from pure grants to taking financial stakes in companies to protect taxpayers.
    * **Intel Example:** The U.S. modified Intel's payout model from a 20% grant to a 4% grant but increased the build commitment to over $500 billion. The government now holds roughly 430 million shares of Intel, turning a potential $10 billion cost into a $30 billion asset.
* **Foreign Investment & Tariffs:** The U.S. secured $550 billion from Japan and $200 billion from South Korea for domestic construction projects.
    * **Trade Levers:** Lutnick revealed that the 25% tariff on Japanese cars was reduced to 15% specifically in exchange for these massive infrastructure investments.
    * **USMCA Reimagining:** Lutnick expressed skepticism toward the current USMCA, suggesting it may need to be "re-addressed" to prevent it from being used to move American auto plants to Mexico.

## AI and the "Genesis Mission" for Science
* **The Genesis Mission:** Under Secretary Dario Gil described this flagship initiative to double the productivity of the U.S. R&D ecosystem within a decade by unifying semiconductors, AI supercomputing, and quantum computing.
    * **Discovery Acceleration:** AI is being used to move science beyond language into mathematics and physics. Gil cited "AlphaFold" as a benchmark, which solved 200 million protein structures in two years—a feat that previously took 50 years to reach just 200,000.
    * **Industrial Partnerships:** The government has formed a "Genesis Consortium" with over 30 partners, including Nvidia and AMD, to build the world’s largest AI supercomputer cluster for science within the national labs.
* **Information Disintermediation:** Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince warned that AI is a platform change that threatens the business model of the internet.
    * **The "Google Problem":** Prince criticized Google for bundling AI training with search rankings, essentially forcing publishers to provide content for free or lose visibility. 
    * **Local Content Value:** High-quality, local, and unique data (e.g., local newspapers like the *Park Record*) is becoming more valuable for AI training than generic national news, potentially creating a "golden era" for niche content creators.

## The Commercial Space and Fusion Race
* **Commercializing Orbit:** Industry leaders are moving toward commercial space stations (e.g., Starlab) to replace the International Space Station (ISS) by the 2030s.
    * **Cost Reduction:** While the ISS cost $450 billion, commercial stations are projected to cost in the "single-digit billions" while offering larger volumes for manufacturing and microgravity research.
    * **Strategic Assets:** Space is being viewed as a tool for global economic efficiency (worth $1T to $10T in value creation) and a source of rare materials like Helium-3 from the moon for fusion energy.
* **The Fusion Timeline:** Bob Mumgaard (Commonwealth Fusion Systems) expects a demonstration plant to be operational by 2027, with commercial power on the grid in the early 2030s.
    * **Competition with China:** Mumgaard warned that while the U.S. leads in science, China is outspending the U.S. on fusion industrial policy by an order of magnitude, threatening U.S. leadership in the "fusion race."

## Global Shifts: India and the Global South
* **India’s Resilience:** Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran (Chief Economic Advisor of India) stated that India is successfully navigating energy shocks by diversifying into nuclear, renewables, and domestic coal.
    * **AI and Labor:** Nageswaran downplayed fears of AI-driven job losses, arguing that the replacement of humans in IT and services will be slower than predicted due to legal and compliance requirements.
* **Leapfrogging the Grid:** In the Global South, the goal is to skip traditional centralized power grids in favor of AI-managed microgrids. 
    * **Distributed Energy:** Manoj Sinha (Husk Power) argued that AI-powered decentralized resources could solve energy access for 300 million people, treating "green electrons" as the foundation for a local industrial revolution in Africa and India.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "When you come to my office and the wall is full of shovels, I promise you we’re at six percent GDP growth... That’s 2027, 2028." — **Howard Lutnick**, U.S. Secretary of Commerce

> "What if I told you the balance sheet of the United States of America was worth five hundred trillion dollars?... You put a businessman in the White House, you put a businessman as the Secretary of Commerce, you’re going to make money using our economy." — **Howard Lutnick**, U.S. Secretary of Commerce

> "Everything that’s wrong with the world today is Google’s fault... they begat Facebook which begat TikTok which begat basically us chasing this deity which is traffic. Traffic is a terrible proxy for quality." — **Matthew Prince**, CEO of Cloudflare

> "The U.S. has been a historic leader in fusion science... however, we don’t really have an industrial policy for fusion. China has a program you can photograph from outer space... we are at risk of losing this race." — **Bob Mumgaard**, CEO of Commonwealth Fusion Systems

briefings.title: LIVE: President Trump gives Tax Day remarks, participates in a roundtable — 4/16/2026
briefings.tldr: President Trump highlighted the impact of the 2025 "great big beautiful" tax bill, which has led to record-high tax refunds for workers through the elimination of taxes on tips, overtime, and Social Security, while incentivizing domestic manufacturing through auto-loan deductions and tariffs.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
President Trump highlighted the impact of the 2025 "great big beautiful" tax bill, which has led to record-high tax refunds for workers through the elimination of taxes on tips, overtime, and Social Security, while incentivizing domestic manufacturing through auto-loan deductions and tariffs.

## Key Tax Reforms and Financial Relief
* **Tax-Free Income Categories:** The administration highlighted three major pillars of the recent tax legislation aimed at working families and seniors:
    * **No Tax on Tips:** Specifically targeted at hospitality hubs like Las Vegas; workers reported refunds ranging from $5,000 to $8,000.
    * **No Tax on Overtime:** Claimed by more than 26 million Americans to date.
    * **No Tax on Social Security:** Over 51 million seniors now pay zero federal tax on their Social Security income.
* **Average Refunds:** Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent reported that the average refund this season is over $4,000, exceeding initial administration expectations.
* **Estate and Small Business Relief:** The bill effectively eliminated the "death tax" (inheritance tax) for small businesses and farms to prevent heirs from having to mortgage or sell properties to pay tax bills.
* **Withholding Adjustments:** Secretary Bessent urged workers to update their withholding levels to see an immediate "surge" in take-home pay rather than waiting for annual refunds.

## New Savings Initiatives and Deductions
* **Trump Accounts:** In partnership with Michael and Susan Dell (who contributed over $6 billion), the government has launched "Trump Accounts" to build generational wealth.
    * **Newborn Seeding:** The Treasury seeds these accounts with a $1,000 contribution for every child born during the term; 5 million accounts have already been opened.
    * **Growth Potential:** The initiative aims to provide children with up to $100,000 by the time they reach adulthood.
* **Auto Loan Interest Deduction:** A new provision allows Americans to deduct the interest paid on car loans, provided the vehicle is **American-made**.
    * Over one million Americans have already utilized this deduction, seeing an average write-off of over $2,000.

## Domestic Manufacturing and Energy
* **Trade and Tariffs:** The President emphasized the use of tariffs to encourage foreign companies to build plants within the U.S., specifically noting a massive influx of pharmaceutical and automotive manufacturing.
* **Energy Production:** The U.S. currently produces more oil than Russia and Saudi Arabia combined, with projections to double that lead by 2027.
* **Stock Market Performance:** The Dow Jones Industrial Average recently reached the 50,000-point milestone.

## Social Policy and Community Impact
* **Education Freedom:** The tax bill expanded school choice and made home-schooling expenditures tax-deductible via federal tax credit scholarships.
* **Women’s Sports:** Trump reiterated his administration’s stance against allowing biological men to participate in women’s sports, characterizing it as a top-tier priority for protecting opportunities for female athletes.
* **Public Safety:** The President claimed the lowest murder rate since 1900 and highlighted the elimination of taxes on overtime for first responders to support local law enforcement.

## Geopolitical and Military Updates
* **Conflict with Iran:** The President reported significant military success in the ongoing conflict, claiming the destruction of 158 Iranian ships and the elimination of key terrorist leaders.
* **Military Technology:** Trump touted the effectiveness of U.S. missile defense systems, noting a recent engagement where 111 incoming rockets were successfully intercepted.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "This is the birthplace of a little idea known as 'No Tax on Tips.'... It was not an expensive consultant. A young waitress came up to me during dinner and she said, 'Sir, we should have no tax on tips.' I said, 'That’s the greatest thing I’ve ever heard.'" — **President Donald J. Trump**

> "Under President Trump, we are celebrating how much more money hard-working Americans will keep, not how much the government will take. Within 24 months, President Trump's idea became the law of the land." — **Scott Bessent, Secretary of the Treasury**

> "With the passage of the great big beautiful bill, my wife and I have benefited from the elimination of taxes on overtime, allowing us to stretch every dollar in an increasingly expensive world. With less financial stress, I'm able to be a better and effective asset to my community." — **Cruz Littlefield, Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Officer**

> "In Nevada, we have what is called a tip compliance... the IRS comes in and they say, 'You're going to make this amount of tips... and we're going to tax you on that even if you don't make that amount.' So to see [no tax on tips] come to fruition was amazing. It is promises made, promises kept." — **Nicole Williams, Culinary Worker**

briefings.title: Michael Howell: We Are Coming To An Inflection Point — Where Liquidity Is Headed

people.name: Julia La Roche
people.role: Host, The Julia La Roche Show

briefings.tldr: Global liquidity has peaked and is entering a multi-year "downswing" that likely won't bottom until 2027, driven by a "debt-refinancing wall" and a robust real economy that is draining capital away from financial markets.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Global liquidity has peaked and is entering a multi-year "downswing" that likely won't bottom until 2027, driven by a "debt-refinancing wall" and a robust real economy that is draining capital away from financial markets. Investors must transition from speculative risk-taking to defensive positioning, focusing on gold, bond duration, and commodities.

## The Global Liquidity Cycle and the 2027 Trough
* **The 5-6 Year Cycle:** Historically, liquidity moves in predictable waves. The current cycle troughed in late 2022 and is projected to reach its next major bottom in 2027.
* **The "Speculation to Turbulence" Transition:** Howell categorizes the cycle into four phases: Rebound, Calm, Speculation, and Turbulence. Markets are currently late in the "Speculation" phase, moving toward "Turbulence" (the "winter" of the cycle).
* **The Real Economy vs. Financial Markets:** Howell argues that "all money that is anywhere must be somewhere." 
    * **Capital Drainage:** A stronger-than-expected real economy—driven by government spending and AI investment—is absorbing private sector liquidity for working capital, leaving less available for financial assets.
    * **Market Divergence:** While business surveys remain gloomy, the stock market correctly identifies that the underlying economy is robust, though this strength perversely tightens financial liquidity.

## The Debt-Liquidity Nexus and Refinancing Risk
* **Refinancing vs. New Financing:** Roughly 80% of global financial market transactions are debt refinancing rather than new capital raises. The system is essentially a "debt-refinancing mechanism" that requires constant liquidity to function.
* **The Debt Maturity Wall:** During the COVID-19 era, many entities "termed out" their debt at near-zero rates. That debt is now coming due and must be refinanced at significantly higher interest rates, creating a massive burden on available liquidity.
* **The Debt-to-Liquidity Ratio:** The historical equilibrium is roughly 2:1 (debt to liquidity). When this ratio exceeds 210%, refinancing crises typically occur. Central banks have historically responded by "throwing liquidity" at the problem, a trend Howell expects to continue over the long term.

## The Shift from "Fed QE" to "Treasury QE"
* **Stealth Monetization:** Howell highlights a transition from traditional Federal Reserve Quantitative Easing (QE) to "Treasury QE." 
    * **Short-End Issuance:** The U.S. Treasury has shifted its issuance calendar toward short-term bills and notes. Because banks primarily buy this short-dated debt, it effectively monetizes the debt, stimulating the real economy more directly than Fed asset purchases.
* **Targeting Volatility:** The Fed and Treasury appear to be "capping" the MOVE Index (bond volatility). 
    * **The Basis Trade:** High bond volatility forces "haircuts" on collateral in the repo market, shrinking the pool of available credit. By suppressing volatility, policymakers protect the "collateral multiplier" and keep the debt-refinancing machine running.
* **Liquidity Injections:** Despite rhetoric of tightening, the Fed added approximately $500–$600 billion in liquidity since December 2023 via reserve management purchases (RMP) to stabilize repo markets.

## Tactical Asset Allocation for the Downswing
* **Reducing Risk:** Investors should be scaling back on credit and high-beta equities while moving toward late-cycle sectors.
* **Defensive Rotation:** 
    * **Sectors:** Favor consumer staples, utilities, and energy/commodities (which perform well during the late-cycle "speculation" peak).
    * **Safe Assets:** Rebuild "bond duration" as systemic risk rises and investors seek the safety of government debt.
* **The "Debasement Trade" (Core Portfolio):** For long-term portfolios, Howell remains bullish on assets that hedge against monetary inflation and debt monetization:
    * **Gold & Bitcoin:** Both act as hedges against the inevitable long-term monetization of government debt.
    * **Residential Real Estate:** High-quality "prime" real estate remains a preferred long-term store of value.

> "Financial markets today are not new financing mechanisms; they're basically debt refinancing systems. 80% of transactions are essentially debt refinancing transactions." — **Michael Howell**

> "All money that is anywhere must be somewhere. If it's in the real economy and being used for debt refinancing, it's not around for buying equities or risk assets." — **Michael Howell**

> "We are moving into a more difficult phase... the pain of reducing liquidity is going to continue for some time, and we've got to adjust our asset allocation accordingly." — **Michael Howell**

briefings.title: OpenAI's Identity Crisis, Datacenter Wars, Market Up on Iran News, Mamdani's First Tax, Swalwell Out
briefings.tldr: OpenAI is facing an "identity crisis" and strategic pivot toward enterprise as Anthropic’s 10x growth rate threatens its dominance, while the tech industry confronts a rising tide of populism targeting data centers and luxury assets.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** OpenAI is facing an "identity crisis" and strategic pivot toward enterprise as Anthropic’s 10x growth rate threatens its dominance, while the tech industry confronts a rising tide of populism targeting data centers and luxury assets.

## OpenAI’s Identity Crisis and the Enterprise Pivot
* **Competitive Escalation:** OpenAI’s Chief Revenue Officer, Denise Dresser, issued a leaked four-page memo attacking Anthropic’s valuation and revenue metrics.
    * **Revenue Discrepancies:** The memo claims Anthropic’s $30 billion run rate is inflated by ~$8 billion through revenue-sharing agreements with cloud providers.
    * **Growth Rates:** David Sacks noted that while OpenAI is growing at 3–4x annually, Anthropic is growing at 10x, potentially reaching an $80–$100 billion run rate by year-end.
* **Strategic Shift:** OpenAI is pivoting aggressively toward business customers and the "agent platform layer."
    * **Enterprise Focus:** The move is intended to capture scalable revenue from coding and enterprise tokens, which offer higher margins than the $20/month consumer subscription model.
    * **Codex vs. Claude:** Chamath Palihapitiya noted that OpenAI’s "Codex" remains superior for complex, long-horizon coding tasks, even as Anthropic’s "Claude" gains ground in day-to-day reliability.
* **Valuation Concerns:** Investors expressed frustration with OpenAI's lack of focus. With a recent $122 billion funding round, the company may need a $1.2 trillion IPO valuation for the math to work for current backers.

## The Datacenter Wars and Rising Populism
* **Infrastructure Backlash:** Data centers have become the new "attack vector" for populist resentment.
    * **Symbolism of Wealth:** David Friedberg argued that data centers represent the "temples of the wealthy," becoming physical targets for those who feel left behind by the AI boom.
    * **Regulatory Resistance:** Sacks noted that data centers are being contested in approximately 30 states due to concerns over energy consumption and "doomer NIMBYism." 
* **The Ratepayer Protection Pledge:** To combat the narrative that data centers drive up local electricity costs, major tech players are increasingly required to "Bring Their Own Energy" (BYOE) or remain power-neutral to the grid.
* **Sovereign Compute:** Sacks highlighted the strategic importance of building data centers in the Gulf (GCC), noting that the IRGC has threatened these sites because they are seen as critical American strategic assets.

## The "Democratic Machine" and Swalwell’s Exit
* **Coordinated Resignation:** Eric Swalwell’s exit from the California governor’s race and resignation from Congress was characterized as a "lancing of the boil" by the Democratic establishment.
    * **The "Pelosi Factor":** Sacks compared the exit to Joe Biden’s withdrawal, suggesting Nancy Pelosi likely gave Swalwell the "hard way or easy way" ultimatum to prevent a fragmented primary from handing the race to a Republican.
    * **Oppo Research Timing:** Friedberg revealed he heard rumors of the allegations against Swalwell as early as December, suggesting the "Democratic Machine" held the information until it was politically advantageous to force a withdrawal.
* **Congressional Trading:** The panel noted that Ro Khanna has traded over $600 million in stock, outperforming even Nancy Pelosi. Chamath argued that the lack of Reg FD (Fair Disclosure) for Congress allows members to trade on information gathered in committee meetings.

## NYC’s Pied-à-Terre Tax and Market Indicators
* **The "Mamdani Tax":** New York is considering a 3.9% annual tax on second homes (pied-à-terres) valued over $5 million.
    * **Market Impact:** Sacks argued this will crash the luxury market and deter investment, as the tax target is the "most elastic" part of the market.
    * **Capital Flight:** Travis Kalanick and Chamath compared the move to London’s "stamp tax," which caused a "slow bleed" of capital to more hospitable cities like Zurich or Milan.
* **Market Outlook:** The market is currently showing confounding signals.
    * **Valuation Metrics:** Both the "Buffett Index" (Equity/GDP) and the Shiller PE ratio are at historical peaks, suggesting a "risk-off" environment.
    * **AI Efficiency:** While the panel is bullish on AI’s long-term potential, Chamath warned that large enterprises have yet to see "tsunamis of revenue" from AI, calling current agent outputs "slop" that requires significant human-in-the-loop refinement.

> "Growth is king right now... if Anthropic is growing faster than OpenAI by a significant clip, the investors are going to play it forward. Efficiency will outstrip subsidy; you can't keep raising $100 billion rounds forever."
> — **Travis Kalanick**

> "The data center is the pied-à-terre of this space. It is the manifestation that people want to attack and destroy because they don't see the value in AI for their own lives yet."
> — **David Friedberg**

> "Nancy Pelosi went to the President and said, 'We can do things the hard way or the easy way.' I think the same thing happened to Swalwell. He was too dumb to listen, and they did things the hard way."
> — **David Sacks**

> "I'm generally more risk-off right now... I think it is crucial that the SpaceX IPO get done ASAP, and that one of Anthropic or OpenAI front-run the other to get out first."
> — **Chamath Palihapitiya**

briefings.title: The AI Hate is Existential | Everybody's Business
briefings.tldr: Public sentiment toward AI has shifted from optimism to existential dread, leading to physical violence against tech leaders and a "broken" job market where recent college graduates face significant underemployment and a mismatch between education and industry needs.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Public sentiment toward AI has shifted from optimism to existential dread, leading to physical violence against tech leaders and a "broken" job market where recent college graduates face significant underemployment and a mismatch between education and industry needs.

## The Rise of AI Backlash and Physical Threats
Recent events indicate a violent pivot in how the public perceives AI leaders and infrastructure.
* **Violent Incidents:**
    * **Sam Altman (OpenAI CEO):** Targeted in an attempted arson involving a Molotov cocktail at his residence; the suspect, Daniel Moreno Gamma, faces attempted murder charges.
    * **Indianapolis Data Center:** A local councilman who approved a data center had bullets fired at his home with a note reading "no data centers."
* **Public Sentiment Shift:** According to Pew Research, 52% of people are now more concerned than excited about AI, compared to only 10% who are more excited than concerned.
* **Top Public Concerns:** Surprisingly, job loss is not the primary fear.
    * **Erosion of Humanity:** 27% cite the erosion of human abilities and connections.
    * **Information Integrity:** 18% worry about the negative impact on information accuracy.
    * **Job Loss:** Ranked only fifth on the list of primary concerns.
* **Marketing Backfire:** Sarah Frier (Bloomberg Managing Editor) notes that CEOs like Sam Altman have marketed AI as "dangerous" and "nuclear" to justify slow rollouts, which inadvertently stoked existential fear in the public.

## The "Broken" Youth Job Market
The promise of "learning to code" has collided with a surplus of graduates and a contraction in entry-level opportunities.
* **Unemployment Disparity:** The unemployment rate for 18-24-year-olds is approximately 8%, double the general population.
* **The "Learn to Code" Failure:**
    * **Oversupply:** Between 2014 and 2024, entry-level openings for computer science grew by 6%, but the number of graduates in that field grew by 110%.
    * **Underemployment:** Many degree-holders are taking roles that do not require their $200,000 education, a phenomenon that can depress salary growth for a decade.
* **AI Natives vs. AI Dependency:** While the Class of 2026 is fluent in LLMs, Julia Rubin (Businessweek Senior Editor) observes they often lack subject matter expertise and "soft skills," such as presenting the slide decks the AI creates for them.

## The Return of the "Human" Worker
As AI automates technical "grunt work," industries are re-evaluating the value of liberal arts and interpersonal skills.
* **The Management Consulting Crisis:** Firms are concerned that AI-generated "slop" is becoming indistinguishable from junior associate output, leading to a renewed focus on human soft skills.
* **"Learn to Ode":** Julia Rubin notes a shift where companies are once again looking for English majors to provide human intuition and communication skills that AI lacks.
* **Education System Failure:** The current crisis is attributed to a "broken" education system where colleges over-enroll students in popular majors without regard for market capacity.

## The "Mordor" Economy and Corporate Pivots
The high energy demands of AI are creating a feedback loop of rising costs and bizarre corporate rebranding.
* **The Mordor Economy:** Stacy Vanek Smith references the "Mordor" concept (coined by Nate Hagens)—an economy where growth is swallowed by the massive energy needs of data centers and resource extraction.
    * **Energy Poverty:** Low-income households are now spending roughly 20% of their income on energy costs.
* **The Allbirds Pivot:** In a stark example of "AI washing," the struggling sustainable shoe brand Allbirds recently spun off its footwear business to become **Newbird AI**.
    * **Strategy:** The company is pivoting toward "GPUaaS" (GPUs as a Service) and hardware.
    * **Market Reaction:** Despite the lack of an obvious connection between shoes and chips, the stock surged 373% following the announcement.

## Notable Quotes

> "The vast majority of people are not seeing yet the way that AI is enriching them. Instead, they’re seeing the way that it’s taking things away, whether that’s employment or resources, or just the threat that it might one day take something away." — **Sarah Frier, Bloomberg Managing Editor**

> "They [companies] have marketed this technology as... 'really, this is so powerful, we need to roll this out slowly, take our time because if we don’t, the results could be disastrous.' It is the strangest public relations strategy of all time." — **Sarah Frier, Bloomberg Managing Editor**

> "If we’re sort of automating away the grunt work or the sort of technical work, then perhaps the work that is more about being a human is going to be much more important." — **Julia Rubin, Businessweek Senior Editor**

> "We are now living in the Mordor economy... an economy that's all about energy. Energy prices get more expensive, so the economy has to make more energy in order to feed the energy needs, and it becomes like a snake swallowing its own tail." — **Stacy Vanek Smith, Bloomberg Host**

briefings.title: Why the A.I. Backlash Turned Violent in America
briefings.tldr: Public sentiment toward AI is shifting toward radicalization and violence, driven by deep economic anxiety, a perceived lack of democratic oversight, and rising local opposition to massive data center infrastructure.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Public sentiment toward AI is shifting toward radicalization and violence, driven by deep economic anxiety, a perceived lack of democratic oversight, and rising local opposition to massive data center infrastructure.

## Radicalization and Violent Backlash
* **Incidents of Physical Violence:** Recent events suggest a dangerous escalation in anti-AI sentiment from online discourse to physical attacks.
    * **Sam Altman Attack:** A 20-year-old suspect allegedly targeted the OpenAI CEO’s San Francisco home with a Molotov cocktail; the suspect possessed a manifesto opposing AI and a "hit list" of other tech executives and investors.
    * **Indianapolis Shooting:** More than a dozen gunshots were fired at the home of Councilman Ron Gibson following his vote to approve a new data center. A note left at the scene read "no data centers."
* **Trust Deficit:** According to a Stanford AI Index report, public trust in the technology is plummeting. 
    * Only 31% of Americans trust their government to regulate AI responsibly, compared to a global average of 54%.
* **The Rhetoric Bind:** Host Casey Newton argues that AI CEOs have "inflamed" the situation by claiming their products pose an "existential threat" to humanity while simultaneously lobbying against safety regulations (such as California’s transparency bills).

## The "Data Center NIMBY" Movement
* **Legislative Moratoriums:** Local and federal politicians are increasingly moving to block the physical infrastructure required for AI.
    * **Maine:** Passed a temporary moratorium on data centers larger than 20 megawatts until 2027.
    * **Wisconsin:** Voters in Port Washington recently restricted the building of future data centers.
    * **Federal Level:** Bernie Sanders and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez have proposed a national moratorium on data center construction.
* **Economic vs. Environmental Fears:** While some view AI as an economic engine, local opposition is focusing on rising home energy costs, environmental degradation, and noise pollution. 
* **Lever for Change:** Host Kevin Roose notes that blocking data centers is the only "lever" average citizens feel they have left to slow a top-down technological revolution they did not ask for.

## Silicon Valley’s Obsession with Longevity
* **Kara Swisher’s Critique:** In an interview regarding her new documentary, *Kara Swisher Wants to Live Forever*, the veteran journalist characterizes the tech elite’s quest for immortality as a "narcissistic" distraction from systemic issues.
    * **"The Wealth Gap":** Swisher argues that the most effective way to increase longevity is universal healthcare, yet many tech leaders support political movements that reduce public health funding.
    * **Stunts vs. Science:** Swisher dismisses hyperbaric chambers and "biohacking" as "ridiculous" stunts for the rich, while identifying mRNA technology and CRISPR gene editing as the truly promising frontiers of medicine.
* **Healthspan vs. Lifespan:** A central theme of the longevity movement is "collapsing" the period of decline at the end of life so that individuals remain healthy until shortly before death.

## The Automation of the CEO
* **The "Zuck-Bot":** Meta is reportedly building an AI version of Mark Zuckerberg to interact with staff.
    * **Training Data:** The bot is being trained on Zuckerberg’s specific mannerisms, tone, and strategic thinking to help employees feel "connected" to the founder.
    * **C-Suite Utility:** Hosts suggest that AI clones could eventually handle repetitive CEO tasks, such as testifying before foreign parliaments, conducting "pre-calls" for events, or answering routine internal inquiries.
* **Synthetic Media Shift:** The project mirrors a broader shift within Meta platforms (Instagram, Facebook) away from human connection and toward synthetic, AI-generated content.

## Notable Quotes
> "Words have power too... someone said to me yesterday they thought [an article] was coming at a time of great anxiety about AI and that it made things more dangerous for me." — **Sam Altman** (via blog post)

> "No one is going to stop the march of AI with a few stray bullets... but it is the CEOs themselves who have been inflaming the rhetoric... telling us that superintelligence is imminent." — **Casey Newton**

> "Death acceptance makes you live longer. Death denial makes you hateful, tiny, and dying quicker. Scientific." — **Kara Swisher**

> "I think the fear and the expectation among the leaders of these companies is that it will get much worse if and when AI does actually start to cause mass disruption to the labor market." — **Kevin Roose**

briefings.title: Why your CEO mentality is wrong (with investor Byron Deeter) | Masters of Scale
briefings.tldr: Scaling a world-class company requires preserving the "founder magic" through long-term leadership while adopting a "pro-athlete" mentality toward executive health and prioritizing high-conviction "big swings" in transformative sectors like AI.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Scaling a world-class company requires preserving the "founder magic" through long-term leadership while adopting a "pro-athlete" mentality toward executive health and prioritizing high-conviction "big swings" in transformative sectors like AI.

## The Founder’s Path and the "Operator-Investor" Balance
* **The "Trigo" Inflection Point:** Byron Deeter co-founded Trigo Technologies in 1999, betting on cloud computing when it was highly controversial.
    * **Customer Validation:** The turning point occurred when "hard, smart customers" (like Staples) provided public testimonials, proving the cloud model worked.
    * **Strategic Acquisition:** Trigo reached a $50M revenue run rate before being acquired by IBM in 2004, which Deeter describes as one of the largest enterprise software outcomes of that era.
* **The Myth of the "Professional CEO":** While Deeter stepped aside for a CEO at Trigo, he now advises most founders *against* this. 
    * **Founder Magic:** Unique product insight is irreplaceable; replacing a founder is destabilizing and introduces significant risk.
    * **Ideal Structure:** Investors should "hire everyone around the founder" to support their strengths rather than replacing them.
* **The Hippocratic Oath of Venture:** As an investor, Deeter follows a "do no harm" policy.
    * **Avoid Over-Operating:** Investors should not try to fix "okay" companies but instead help "great" companies stay excellent.
    * **High-Velocity Communication:** Deeter prioritizes low-friction, asynchronous communication (WhatsApp, Slack, Signal) over long meetings to stay in the flow of the CEO's day.

## Investment Strategy and the "Anti-Portfolio"
* **Crimes of Omission:** Deeter notes that for top-tier firms, the "missed" deals (like Tesla or Atlassian) hurt more than the investments that fail. 
* **The Anti-Portfolio:** Bessemer publicly lists the great companies they passed on to maintain humility and learn from mistakes.
* **Long-Term Horizons:** Bessemer’s average hold period is approximately 14 years. Deeter seeks "Century Companies"—iconic firms that "dent the space-time continuum."
* **Investment Criteria:** He looks for two primary (and often conflicting) traits in founders:
    * **Intense Conviction:** A bold, unwavering vision.
    * **Coachability:** The ability to seek outbound input when intensity mounts rather than turning inward.

## The AI Transformation: Anthropic and Beyond
* **The New Hyperscalers:** Deeter believes foundation models (like Anthropic) are the new infrastructure, similar to how AWS/Azure were for the first cloud wave.
* **Anthropic Bet:** Bessemer’s investment in Anthropic—their largest check ever—was driven by:
    * **Talent Magnetism:** CEO Dario Amodei's ability to attract the world's best AI researchers.
    * **Ethical AI as a Business Moat:** Their commitment to safety and ethics serves as a magnet for enterprise customers who need a trusted partner.
* **The "One-Person Billion-Dollar Company":** Deeter predicts we will see a billion-dollar company (on its merits, not just financing) with a single employee within "one year and one day."

## CEO Performance: The STRIVE Program
* **CEO as Athlete:** Deeter argues that CEOs often treat their bodies poorly, which is "statistically the same as running a company drunk" due to sleep deprivation.
* **The STRIVE Framework:** Bessemer launched a program focused on sleep, training, and regimen to apply peak-performance principles from the NFL to tech founders.
    * **Mental Health:** Deeter emphasizes normalizing therapy and coaching to prevent "tapping out" under the unprecedented stress of the current market.
    * **The "Power Bar" Fallacy:** Reflecting on his own days as a CEO (where he ended up with 13 cavities from living on protein bars), Deeter advocates for better sleep and nutrition as high-ROI business strategies.
